citation: README.md desiderata, sessions outlive the app; docs/architecture.md, durability; kan a_28YgGqYq7
why:
Muster's daemon is started by whichever shell started Muster, and it outlives that shell, that window and that app. Every pane it ever spawns is its child, so whatever it was handed at birth becomes permanent state handed to every agent - which for a tool whose entire purpose is running coding agents is close to the worst place for a stray variable to end up.

That is not hypothetical. Launching Muster from inside a Claude Code session put that session's CLAUDE_CODE_* markers and its messaging credentials into the daemon; a fresh Claude Code started in a pane read them, silently turned its own transcript saving off, and held another session's IPC token. It persisted after that Muster had quit.

So the daemon is handed an allowlist rather than an inheritance. A denylist would have to keep up with every tool that invents a variable, and would be wrong until somebody noticed - which is the same shape of failure again.

The list is short on purpose, and the reason is worth stating: a pane runs a shell, and a shell rebuilds its own world from the user's rc files. Toolchain managers, version switchers and prompts all put themselves back. What has to survive is only what a shell cannot work out for itself - where home is, what to run, and the machine's conventions.

Cases below name the whole environment a launch might carry and say which of it reaches the daemon. `carried` is name=value so that a case can show a value surviving intact; `dropped` is names alone.

`supplied` is what Muster adds that nobody handed it: a locale when the launch named none, and Muster's own command directory at the front of PATH.

A daemon on another machine is started from that machine's own environment as an ssh session there sees it, through the same allowlist less SSH_AUTH_SOCK (`far`). Nothing is supplied there, since the locale and the command directory are this machine's answers.

cases.name: a harness's session state does not reach the daemon
cases.why: The bug this exists for, in the shape it was found. CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION told a fresh agent it was a child session and to stop saving its transcript; CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN handed it another session's credentials. Neither belongs to the agents Muster runs - they belonged to whoever launched Muster - and both would have outlived the app that carried them in.

cases.name: where a pane's tools keep their config survives
cases.why: A pane's tools read their config, state and caches from the XDG directories, and a login shell does not set them: they come from whatever the person's session exported. Dropped, and every tool in every pane falls back to its defaults under HOME, quietly ignoring the configuration its owner pointed it at, for as long as the daemon runs.

cases.name: a pane gets a shell that works
cases.why:
The other half of the allowlist, and the reason it is not simply HOME. A daemon with no PATH spawns a shell that cannot run `ls`; one with no SHELL has nothing to spawn. USER and LOGNAME are what a git author or a home-directory lookup reads, and no shell can invent them.

TERM is here to be dropped, and that is a deliberate absence rather than an oversight. No pane ever sees the daemon's: herdr sets TERM=xterm-256color per pane unconditionally, because a pane is rendered by herdr's own terminal layer rather than by whatever launched the app. The one thing that does read the daemon's own is herdr's host-terminal detection, which decides who a notification is attributed to - so carrying xterm-ghostty meant a daemon posting notifications as Ghostty, to a terminal that is not there. Dropping it also makes a terminal launch and a Dock launch give the daemon the same environment, and a Dock launch never had one.

cases.name: the whole locale family travels together
cases.why: Carrying some of the locale is worse than carrying none: a pane with LANG set and LC_CTYPE not renders wide glyphs differently from the terminal it was launched from, which reads as a font bug rather than a missing variable. LC_ is a prefix rather than a list because the family is open - a machine can set LC_MEASUREMENT and LC_TELEPHONE - and a list would be wrong on somebody's machine and silent about it.

cases.name: the user's ssh agent travels, deliberately
cases.why: A credential channel carried on purpose, which is worth writing down so it reads as a decision rather than a hole in the list. A pane that cannot `git push` or reach a devenv is a pane somebody stops using, every terminal emulator on this platform passes this through, and unlike a harness's session token it belongs to the person rather than to whichever program happened to launch Muster.

cases.name: a person's own herdr does not come along
cases.why: HERDR_SOCKET_PATH and HERDR_SESSION name a herdr daemon, which is a person's own and nothing of Muster's. Carrying either would point a pane's own `herdr` CLI at a daemon chosen by whoever happened to launch Muster, rather than the one its owner's shell profile names.

cases.name: a shell's own accumulated world is left for the shell to rebuild
cases.why: This is what keeps the list short. A login shell re-reads the user's rc files inside the pane, so a version manager, a language toolchain and a prompt all put themselves back - carrying them would freeze one moment's answer into a daemon that outlives every window, so a person who changed their setup would keep getting the old one until they found and killed the daemon.

cases.name: a variable set to nothing is not carried
cases.why: An empty value and an unset name mean the same thing to everything that reads one, and the rest of Muster already treats them alike when resolving a socket path. Passing the empty one through would make a daemon that has HOME set to nothing look different from one that has no HOME, which is a distinction nobody wants to debug.

cases.name: an empty environment carries nothing, rather than inventing a floor
cases.why: A launch from something that cleared its environment is not a launch worth guessing at. Inventing a HOME or a PATH here would put the guess in a process that outlives the app; letting it through empty means the socket path resolves to nothing and the launch says so, which is the failure everybody can act on.

cases.name: a window launched from the Dock is given the locale nobody gave it
cases.why:
launchd hands a GUI process the environment below and nothing more - no LANG, no LC_* - so the allowlist has no locale to carry and a daemon started from it would run in the C locale, handing that to every pane it spawns. That is exactly what LANG is on the list to prevent, and an allowlist cannot carry what is absent. The environment here is measured rather than imagined: a bundle opened under `env -i`, which is the closest thing to a double-click a script can arrange.

Worth knowing why nothing looks broken in the app today. Building the renderer calls Ghostty's own ensureLocale, which derives a locale from CFLocale and setenvs it into the whole process before Muster starts its daemon - so the daemon gets one by way of the renderer. That is a loan of the same kind as the fonts and colours Muster used to take from a Ghostty config, and less visible: it depends on the renderer being built first, and a renderer that stopped doing it would drop every pane to the C locale in silence. This case is Muster's own answer, which is why it is here rather than left to a dependency.

cases.name: a window launched from a terminal keeps the locale it was handed
cases.why: The other launch, and the reason this is not simply 'always set LANG'. A shell exports its own, and the value a person has configured beats one derived from a system setting they may never have looked at - so what the platform says is only consulted when nothing else answered.

cases.name: a locale that is half set is left half set rather than completed
cases.why: Carrying some of the locale family is worse than carrying none, which is why LC_ is a prefix in the allowlist. Supplying a LANG beside an inherited LC_CTYPE would create exactly that split from the other direction: a daemon whose ctype and whose language were decided by different machines. Whoever set one variable and not the others meant something by it, and this is not the place to guess what.

cases.name: a platform that will not name a locale has none invented for it
cases.why: The same rule the empty environment gets: what cannot be answered is left unanswered. A locale written down here would be a transcription of somebody else's machine, put into a process that outlives the app and handed to every pane it ever spawns. The C locale is at least honest about being a default.

cases.name: a pane can reach the muster command belonging to its own window
cases.why: The whole of how an agent in a pane comes to be able to drive the window it is drawn in. Every pane is a child of the daemon, so the daemon's PATH is the pane's PATH, and Muster's own command directory goes on the front of it. In front rather than behind, so a pane reaches the CLI of the window it is in rather than one somebody installed years ago; macOS path_helper appends to an inherited PATH rather than replacing it, so the entry survives a pane's login shell. PATH is in both lists here, which is the honest description of a variable that was inherited and then added to - and this is the list somebody reads when `muster` is not found in a pane.

cases.name: a directory already on the PATH is not put there twice
cases.why: Anybody who added this to their own shell profile would otherwise have it prepended again on every launch, and a daemon adopted from an earlier Muster hands its PATH to every pane it ever spawns. The entry is already doing its job; a second copy only makes the value longer and the log harder to read.

cases.name: an empty PATH is left empty rather than filled with one entry
cases.why: A PATH holding only Muster's commands is a pane whose shell cannot run `ls`, which is worse than a pane with no `muster` in it - and nothing here can honestly say what the rest of the PATH should be. An empty value is not carried either, so the shell in that pane builds its own from scratch, which is what it did before this existed.

cases.name: a build that staged no command changes nobody's PATH
cases.why: The state a checkout without a staged CLI is in, and it has to be a quiet one: the window works exactly as it did before any of this existed, and a pane simply finds no `muster`. Inventing a directory to name would put a path on every daemon's PATH that holds nothing.

cases.name: a daemon on another machine does not carry the connection that started it
cases.why: A remote daemon is started over one ssh connection and outlives it. On the far side SSH_AUTH_SOCK names that connection's agent forwarding, a path unique to it that is gone the moment it ends, so a pane handed it would find its agent missing after the next reconnect. The ssh session's own variables were never on the list, and they are named here because this is where they arrive.
